name: 3-Step
summary: South African house hybrid built around three kick hits per bar instead of four - the missing kick, not a new sound, is the hook. Amapiano's log-drum bassline and Afro-Tech's punchy percussion loops fill the space around the gap, over a heavy 55-65% shuffle that reads as conversational and jazz-like rather than mechanical.

sounds.kick: Warm, rounded mid-deep-house kick (LinnDrum/DMX lineage, or a tighter 909 for the Afro-Tech-leaning grooves) with a short transient so the missing beat reads as real silence.
sounds.snare: Rarely a snare in the house sense - claps and rims (perc/rim slots) carry the backbeat, understated and often syncopated rather than locked to 2 and 4.
sounds.hats: Sharp closed hats kept under ~70% velocity on the Afro-Tech-driven grooves; largely absent on the deep-house-leaning ones where the shaker and log drum carry the groove instead.
sounds.percussion: The genre's real engine: a swung shaker/tambourine timekeeper, a tomLow+congaLow 'log drum' rhythm approximation (Amapiano influence), and clave/conga call-and-response (Afro-Tech influence) filling the gap the missing kick leaves behind.
sounds.cymbals: Almost absent - horn stabs (perc slot) and pads carry the energy a cymbal wash would in other genres; a soft ride appears only in breakdowns.

machines: Roland TR-909 - tighter kick, closed/open hat, ride for the Afro-Tech-leaning grooves
E-mu SP-1200 - lo-fi resampled kick and hats
Roland TR-727 - clave, cowbell, conga and shaker patches for the percussion timeline
Roland CR-78 - softer analogue conga/bongo tones
Korg KR-55 / KPR-77 - period-adjacent latin percussion rims and hats
Elektron Machinedrum - metallic hat alternative for the harder Afro-Tech grooves
Real congas/djembe/shakers and a synth/sampled log-drum patch - the genuine pitched log drum and live hand percussion this drum-only library cannot reproduce
Horn/brass stab samples for the perc-slot 'jazzy horns'
